Other Features

Additional features and utilities.

cdrl

Contract Deliverables (CDRL/SDRL) and Verification & Validation (V&V) API router.

This module provides the API endpoints for managing contract deliverables and V&V test cases within the Eisenhower Portfolio Manager.

Contract Deliverables

In defence contracting, every contract specifies a set of formal deliverables (CDRLs — Contract Data Requirements List, or SDRLs — Supplier Data Requirements List) that must be produced, submitted, reviewed, and accepted. Each deliverable follows a lifecycle from DRAFTING through SUBMITTED, UNDER_REVIEW, and finally ACCEPTED (or REJECTED).

The review window is a critical tracking metric: once a deliverable is submitted, the contracting authority has a defined number of days to review it. These endpoints expose countdown queries so programme managers can see which reviews are approaching their deadline.

Verification & Validation

V&V test cases provide objective, physical completion gates. Before a work package can be marked as 100% complete, all mandatory test cases must be in either PASSED or WAIVED status. The V&V gate check endpoint is used by the progress update flow to enforce this interlock.

Billing Milestone Interlock

Billing milestones linked to CDRLs cannot transition to complete while the CDRL status is REJECTED or UNDER_REVIEW. This check is performed in the V&V gate check endpoint.

Endpoints

CDRL Operations:

GET /api/v1/cdrl/ — List all deliverables with optional filtering. POST /api/v1/cdrl/ — Create a new deliverable. GET /api/v1/cdrl/{id} — Get a single deliverable. PUT /api/v1/cdrl/{id} — Update a deliverable (status transitions, submission). DELETE /api/v1/cdrl/{id} — Delete a deliverable. GET /api/v1/cdrl/countdown — List deliverables with review deadlines approaching.

V&V Test Case Operations:

GET /api/v1/cdrl/node/{node_id}/vv-tests — List V&V test cases for a node. POST /api/v1/cdrl/node/{node_id}/vv-tests — Create a V&V test case. PUT /api/v1/cdrl/vv-tests/{id} — Update a V&V test case status. DELETE /api/v1/cdrl/vv-tests/{id} — Delete a V&V test case.

V&V Gate Check:

GET /api/v1/cdrl/node/{node_id}/vv-gate-check — Check if a node can complete.

Comments

Comments router for task-level discussion threads.

This module provides REST endpoints for creating, reading, updating, and deleting comments attached to tasks within the portfolio management system. Comments allow team members to discuss task details, share updates, and maintain an audit trail of decisions.

Warning

This router uses the legacy relational data model (Task, Project, Portfolio) and is not imported by the main FastAPI application. It is retained for reference only. The current system uses the unified UniversalBreakdownNode tree structure with the WBS router (app.routers.wbs).

Endpoints

Access Control

Comments are accessible only to users who have membership in the portfolio that contains the task’s project. Only the comment author may edit or delete their own comments; administrators may delete any comment.

db_health

Database health and maintenance API router.

This module exposes the /api/v1/admin/db-health endpoint for querying database health metrics and triggering maintenance tasks. It provides administrators with visibility into replication lag, index fragmentation, table bloat, and WAL archiving status.

Endpoints

  • GET /api/v1/admin/db-health — Returns current database health metrics without running maintenance.

  • POST /api/v1/admin/db-health/run-maintenance — Triggers a full maintenance run (VACUUM ANALYZE, re-index) and returns the results.

Security

All endpoints require JWT authentication. In production, these endpoints should be accessible only to administrators with clearance ≥ SECRET.

The maintenance tasks require superuser privileges on the PostgreSQL database. In a Patroni HA cluster, maintenance should be run only on the primary node.

facilities

Facility reservation and timeline API endpoints.

This router provides endpoints for managing chamber reservations and viewing facility timelines. It is the primary interface for booking high-demand physical resources (EMC Anechoic Chambers, Thermal Vacuum Chambers, HIL rigs) and checking their availability.

Endpoints

  • POST /reservations — Create a new chamber reservation with full validation (capability gate, calibration gate, buffer enforcement).

  • GET /locations/{id}/timeline — Retrieve the time-phased reservation timeline for a facility, including buffer/cooldown slots.

Security

All endpoints require JWT authentication via app.utils.auth.get_current_user(). The authenticated user’s clearance level is checked against the facility’s security classification before returning reservation data.

Line Management

Line management, leave booking, and resource downtime API router.

This module exposes REST endpoints for:

  1. Line Management — Setting and querying reporting relationships.

  2. Leave Requests — Submitting, approving, rejecting, and cancelling leave.

  3. Leave Impact Assessment — Checking team overlap and delivery risk.

  4. Resource Downtime — Scheduling and managing physical resource offline periods.

  5. Skills Management — Querying and managing user skill profiles.

Endpoints

Line Management

  • GET /api/v1/line-management/my-manager — Get current user’s line manager.

  • GET /api/v1/line-management/my-reports — Get direct reports of current user.

  • GET /api/v1/line-management/all-reports — Get all direct and indirect reports.

  • GET /api/v1/line-management/chain-of-command — Get full chain of command.

  • GET /api/v1/line-management/hierarchy — Get nested team hierarchy tree.

  • PUT /api/v1/line-management/set-manager/{user_id} — Set a user’s line manager (admin).

Leave Requests

  • POST /api/v1/leave/requests — Submit a new leave request.

  • GET /api/v1/leave/my-requests — Get current user’s leave requests.

  • GET /api/v1/leave/pending — Get pending requests for current user’s reports.

  • POST /api/v1/leave/{id}/approve — Approve a pending leave request.

  • POST /api/v1/leave/{id}/reject — Reject a pending leave request.

  • POST /api/v1/leave/{id}/cancel — Cancel own pending leave request.

  • GET /api/v1/leave/overlap-assessment — Assess team leave overlap risk.

Resource Downtime

  • POST /api/v1/downtime — Schedule resource offline period.

  • GET /api/v1/downtime — List upcoming downtime records.

  • GET /api/v1/downtime/{resource_id} — Get downtime for a specific resource.

  • DELETE /api/v1/downtime/{id} — Cancel a scheduled downtime.

Skills

  • GET /api/v1/skills — List all skill definitions.

  • GET /api/v1/skills/categories — List all skill categories.

  • GET /api/v1/skills/my-skills — Get current user’s skill profiles.

  • POST /api/v1/skills/add — Add or update a skill for current user.

  • DELETE /api/v1/skills/{skill_id} — Remove a skill from current user.

Milestones

Milestones router for project milestone tracking.

This module provides REST endpoints for creating, reading, updating, and deleting milestones associated with projects. Milestones represent key date-driven checkpoints in a project schedule, such as design reviews, contractual delivery dates, or phase gate approvals.

Warning

This router uses the legacy relational data model (Milestone, Project, Portfolio) and is not imported by the main FastAPI application. It is retained for reference only. The current system uses the unified UniversalBreakdownNode tree structure with milestone weight steps managed by the EVM router (app.routers.evm).

Endpoints

Method

Description

GET /milestones/

List milestones with optional filters.

POST /milestones/

Create a new milestone.

GET /milestones/{id}

Get a single milestone by ID.

PUT /milestones/{id}

Update a milestone.

DELETE /milestones/{id}

Delete a milestone.

GET /milestones/project/{id} | Get all milestones for a project.

Access Control

Milestones are accessible only to users who have membership in the portfolio that contains the milestone’s project. Viewers cannot create, update, or delete milestones.

dev: mock fixtures

Developer mock fixtures — reproducible test scenarios for UI integration.

This module provides seed data scenarios that populate the database with realistic, defence-domain test data for rapid frontend development and integration testing. Each scenario is a self-contained programme with 50+ nodes, PDM dependency links, 3-point Monte Carlo estimates, resource assignments, simulated clashes, and baseline snapshots.

Scenarios are designed to exercise every UI component in the HMI catalog:

  • Gantt chart: Multi-level WBS with planned/actual dates, progress, blockers, cross-hatch shading, and baseline comparisons.

  • Jagged drop line: Mix of ahead, on-track, behind, and complete tasks.

  • Daily cockpit: Active sprint load, blocked items, urgent tasks, focus queue, and claimable placeholder tasks.

  • Clash triage: Resource double-bookings, clearance lapses, and facility collisions with proposed leveling shifts.

  • Display settings: Server-side profile hydration on login.

Available Scenarios

  1. avionics-radar — Avionics radar development programme with 50 nodes spanning requirements, design, development, integration, and test phases. Includes PDM links (FS/SS/FF/SF), 3-point estimates, resource assignments, and simulated clashes.

  2. minimal — Small 10-node scenario for quick smoke testing of the Gantt chart and basic cockpit views.

Usage

In development environments, call:

GET /api/v1/dev/fixtures/avionics-radar

This clears and repopulates the database with the scenario data, returning a summary of what was seeded. The endpoint is only available when ``ENVIRONMENT != ‘production’`` to prevent accidental data loss.

Security Warning

This endpoint is DANGEROUS — it clears existing data. It is gated behind the ENVIRONMENT setting and will not load in production. Never expose this endpoint in a production deployment.

Portfolios

Portfolios router for top-level programme container management.

This module provides REST endpoints for creating, reading, updating, and deleting portfolios, as well as managing portfolio membership. Portfolios are the highest-level containers in the legacy data model, grouping related projects under a common governance structure.

Warning

This router uses the legacy relational data model (Portfolio, PortfolioMember) and is not imported by the main FastAPI application. It is retained for reference only. The current system uses the unified UniversalBreakdownNode tree structure with the WBS router (app.routers.wbs).

Endpoints

Access Control

Portfolios are accessible to their owner and all members. Only the owner or members with edit roles can modify portfolio settings or manage membership.

Projects

Projects router for mid-level project container management.

This module provides REST endpoints for creating, reading, updating, and deleting projects within portfolios. Projects sit between portfolios and tasks in the legacy hierarchy, representing discrete work efforts with their own managers, statuses, and priorities.

Warning

This router uses the legacy relational data model (Project, Portfolio) and is not imported by the main FastAPI application. It is retained for reference only. The current system uses the unified UniversalBreakdownNode tree structure with the WBS router (app.routers.wbs).

Endpoints

Method

Description

GET /projects/

List accessible projects.

POST /projects/

Create a new project.

GET /projects/{id}

Get a single project by ID.

PUT /projects/{id}

Update a project.

DELETE /projects/{id}

Delete a project.

GET /projects/{id}/stats | Get project statistics (task counts).

Access Control

Projects are accessible to users who have membership in the containing portfolio. Only the portfolio owner, project manager, or non-viewer members can edit projects.

Tasks

Tasks router for work item management within projects.

This module provides REST endpoints for creating, reading, updating, and deleting tasks within projects. Tasks are the lowest-level work items in the legacy data model, representing individual units of work with assignees, priorities, statuses, and due dates.

Warning

This router uses the legacy relational data model (Task, Project, Portfolio) and is not imported by the main FastAPI application. It is retained for reference only. The current system uses the unified UniversalBreakdownNode tree structure with the WBS router (app.routers.wbs).

Endpoints

Method

Description

GET /tasks/

List tasks with various filters.

POST /tasks/

Create a new task.

GET /tasks/{id}

Get a single task by ID.

PUT /tasks/{id}

Update a task.

DELETE /tasks/{id}

Delete a task.

Access Control

Tasks are accessible to users who have membership in the portfolio containing the task’s project, or to the task’s direct assignee. Only the portfolio owner, project manager, or non-viewer members can create, update, or delete tasks.

custom_fields

Admin router for Custom Field Definition CRUD operations.

This module provides the API endpoints for managing custom field definitions in the portfolio management system. Only users with PMO_DIRECTOR or SYSTEM_ADMIN roles can create, update, or delete field definitions.

Endpoints

  • GET /custom-fields — List definitions (filterable by target_entity).

  • POST /custom-fields — Create a new definition.

  • GET /custom-fields/{id} — Get a single definition.

  • PUT /custom-fields/{id} — Update an existing definition.

  • DELETE /custom-fields/{id} — Soft-deactivate a definition.

Access Control

All endpoints require JWT authentication. Create, update, and delete operations require the SYSTEM_ADMIN role. List and get operations are available to all authenticated users.

Usage

from app.routers.admin.custom_fields import router

app.include_router(router, prefix="/api/v1/admin")

See Also

  • app.models.custom_fields — CustomFieldDefinition model.

  • app.schemas.custom_fields — Pydantic schemas.

  • app.services.custom_field_engine — Validation engine.
